verdict.rationale: cubic's docs say users can tag @cubic-dev-ai or reply in PR comments to ask questions, trigger reviews and fix issues, and plain-English replies teach it what to do differently. Its MCP server also lets a coding agent request reviews, triage issues and manage seats and subscriptions from natural-language prompts. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of natural-language command handling, and evidence that core configuration (e.g. cubic.yaml settings) can be done via natural language rather than files and UI.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Interact with cubic in PR comments to ask questions, trigger reviews, and fix issues. You can tag `@cubic-dev-ai` directly, or reply to cubic's existing comments to continue the conversation.
Reply to its comments: Type a response explaining what cubic should do differently, and it remembers for next time
You can now ask your coding agent to check your cubic subscription, manage team seats and roles, and purchase more seats without leaving your MCP client.
When a pull request needs extra scrutiny, you can ask cubic for an Ultrareview.
